title: A stiff back
context: A 38-year-old man has had years of morning back stiffness that eases with exercise. He also had a red, painful eye last year.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Stevenfruitsmaak
img.alt: Thin, smooth bony bridges (syndesmophytes) join the vertebrae into a continuous column

hints: Look at the shape of the spine: smooth, joined-up edges.
The vertebrae have fused into one long column that looks like a plant stem.
why: Thin, smooth bony bridges (syndesmophytes) join the vertebrae into a continuous column: a 'bamboo spine'.
assoc: Inflammatory back pain in young adults
pearl: Inflammatory back pain improves with exercise and is worse with rest and in the early morning. Treat early: modern biologics can prevent fusion.

title: Dull on one side
context: A 41-year-old with weeks of cough, night sweats and weight loss is now breathless. One lung base is dull to percussion.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.file: Pleural effusion of primary pulmonary tuberculosis.jpg
img.author: Basem Abbas Al Ubaidi
img.alt: A dense white opacity at the left base with a curved upper edge rising towards the side wall (meniscus sign), obscuring the diaphragm

hints: The white area hides the diaphragm and the costophrenic angle.
Its upper edge curves up at the side, like a meniscus.
why: A dense white opacity at the left base with a curved upper edge rising towards the side wall (meniscus sign), obscuring the diaphragm: a pleural effusion, here from tuberculosis.
pearl: Tap it if you don't know why it's there. Light's criteria separate exudates from transudates. In many countries, TB is a leading cause of exudative effusion in young adults.

title: A fall on the hand
context: A 72-year-old woman slipped on wet tiles and landed on her outstretched hand. Her wrist looks like a dinner fork.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Lucien Monfils
img.alt: A fracture of the distal radius with the broken fragment angled backwards (dorsally)

hints: The break is in the radius, just above the wrist.
On the side view, which way has the broken end tipped?
why: A fracture of the distal radius with the broken fragment angled backwards (dorsally): the 'dinner fork' deformity of a Colles fracture.
pearl: A low-energy wrist fracture in an older person is often the first sign of osteoporosis, so consider bone density testing. A Smith fracture tips the other way (forwards).

title: Recurrent infections
context: A 58-year-old woman has had repeated urinary infections and loin aches. Plain X-ray of the abdomen:
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Nevit Dilmen
img.alt: A large, branching radio-opaque stone filling the renal pelvis and calyces of one kidney, shaped like a stag's antlers.

hints: There's a large white, branched shape over one kidney.
It fills the renal pelvis and branches into the calyces, like antlers.
why: A large, branching radio-opaque stone filling the renal pelvis and calyces of one kidney, shaped like a stag's antlers.
assoc: Struvite stones from urease-producing bacteria (e.g. Proteus)
pearl: Staghorn calculi are usually infection stones and can destroy the kidney if left. They usually need removal (often percutaneous nephrolithotomy) plus treatment of the infection.

title: A child's elbow
context: A 7-year-old fell off the monkey bars onto an outstretched hand and won't move the elbow.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: James Heilman, MD
img.alt: A fracture across the lower humerus just above the condyles, with some displacement of the lower fragment.

hints: Look just above the elbow joint, at the lower end of the humerus.
Compare the alignment of the humerus with the capitellum.
why: A fracture across the lower humerus just above the condyles, with some displacement of the lower fragment.
assoc: Fall on an outstretched hand in children (5–7 years)
pearl: The commonest elbow fracture in children. Always check the radial pulse and nerves (especially the anterior interosseous nerve: ask for an 'OK' sign). A raised posterior fat pad suggests a hidden fracture.

title: A bad flare
context: A 29-year-old woman with known ulcerative colitis has bloody diarrhoea, fever, a racing pulse and a tender, swollen abdomen.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Hellerhoff
img.alt: Marked dilatation of the colon (transverse colon over 6 cm) with loss of the normal haustral pattern, in a systemically unwell patient with colitis

hints: The large bowel is very dilated, especially the transverse colon.
Put the X-ray together with fever, tachycardia and her known bowel condition.
why: Marked dilatation of the colon (transverse colon over 6 cm) with loss of the normal haustral pattern, in a systemically unwell patient with colitis: toxic megacolon.
pearl: Toxic megacolon is a surgical emergency with a high risk of perforation. Avoid opioids, antidiarrhoeals and anticholinergics, and involve surgeons early.

title: Coughing for months
context: A 45-year-old has had a productive cough, night sweats and weight loss for three months.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC
img.alt: Patchy shadowing in both upper zones with a thick-walled cavity at the right apex

hints: The changes are worst at the top of the lungs.
There's a hole (cavity) with a thick wall at the right apex.
why: Patchy shadowing in both upper zones with a thick-walled cavity at the right apex: classic post-primary (reactivation) TB.
pearl: Upper-lobe cavitation means a high bacterial load: isolate the patient and send three sputum samples. TB remains one of the world's leading infectious killers.

title: A puffy face and dark urine
context: A 12-year-old had a sore throat three weeks ago. Now he has puffy eyes, cola-coloured urine, high blood pressure and is breathless.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: CDC/Dr Thomas Hooten
img.alt: An enlarged heart shadow with congested lungs (fluid overload) in a child with haematuria, oedema and hypertension weeks after a strep throat

hints: The heart looks big and the lungs look congested.
Put it with the sore throat three weeks ago and the cola-coloured urine.
why: An enlarged heart shadow with congested lungs (fluid overload) in a child with haematuria, oedema and hypertension weeks after a strep throat: acute post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis.
assoc: Group A streptococcal throat or skin infection
pearl: An AP film exaggerates heart size, so be careful calling cardiomegaly on it. Post-strep GN is still common in remote Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, often after skin sores.

title: Fell off his bike
context: A 30-year-old came off his bike onto his shoulder. He has a tender lump over the front of the shoulder.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Majorkev (cropped)
img.alt: A break through the middle third of the collarbone with the ends slightly displaced.

hints: Follow the long bone across the top of the chest.
There's a break in its middle third.
why: A break through the middle third of the collarbone with the ends slightly displaced.
pearl: Most mid-shaft clavicle fractures heal well in a sling. Check the skin over it and the neurovascular status of the arm; shortening, skin tenting or an open wound needs a surgical opinion.

title: Vomiting and a swollen belly
context: A 66-year-old who had bowel surgery years ago has colicky abdominal pain, vomiting and hasn't passed wind for a day.
question: What's the diagnosis?

img.author: Igboeze
img.alt: Multiple dilated, centrally placed bowel loops with air-fluid levels in a 'step-ladder' pattern

hints: Look for stacked loops of bowel with horizontal lines across them.
The dilated loops are central and the lines are air-fluid levels.
why: Multiple dilated, centrally placed bowel loops with air-fluid levels in a 'step-ladder' pattern: small bowel obstruction.
pearl: Adhesions cause most small bowel obstructions in people who've had surgery; hernias are the main cause in those who haven't. Always check the hernial orifices.
